variants.headline: Money in hand, no food to buy
variants.body: Shops and farms are sold out of food, leaving people with money unable to buy meals. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.

variants.headline: Shops and farms sell out
variants.body: People have money for food but cannot buy it because shops and farms are sold out. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.

variants.headline: Food shortage defeats the buyer
variants.body: Food is unavailable to buyers even with money in hand: shops and farms are sold out. The gazette favours fair treatment of {target} rather than an adverse verdict founded upon assumption alone.
